SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints (began ~1.5–2 months ago):
  • Episodic pins-and-needles and numbness in right hand.  
  • Subjective weakness in right arm and right leg during episodes; colleague reports abnormal gait.  
  • Difficulty holding/ drinking from a cup and throat “something there” sensation only during episodes.  
  • Generalized tiredness, weakness, and intermittent nausea.
  • No speech or visual disturbance reported.
  • Episodes initially once per week to once per month, now occurring a couple of times per day (duration described as 3–4 days before resolution – conflict noted).

- Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses.

- Medications:
  • Aspirin 75 mg once daily (self-initiated; dose/route/frequency documented).

- Social history:
  • Occupation: Plastic-surgery physician.  
  • Lives with wife.  
  • Non-smoker.

- Family history:
  • Father: carotid surgery for stroke risk.

- Allergies:
  • Penicillin.

Objective:
- No in-person examination performed (video connection lost).  
- Patient asymptomatic at time of call.  
- No vital signs or physical findings available.

Investigations: None performed to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Episodic unilateral motor/sensory deficits
   - Assessment: Suspected transient ischemic attack (TIA).
   - Differential diagnosis: Migraine aura, focal seizure, multiple sclerosis relapse, cervical radiculopathy.
   - Investigations planned: Urgent TIA clinic work-up (carotid Doppler ultrasound, brain imaging, additional stroke risk blood tests as per clinic protocol).
   - Treatment planned: Continue low-dose aspirin (pending specialist review); emergency advice given to attend ED immediately if symptoms become prolonged or worsened.
   - Referrals: Same-week referral to local TIA/mini-stroke clinic; contact numbers for PALS and clinic provided.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: No documented vitals, cardiovascular/neuro physical exam, or medication reconciliation beyond aspirin.  
● Internal conflicts: Episode frequency now “couple of times a day” vs. duration “3–4 days then resolves.”  
● Transcript quality: Occasional audio dropouts; video feed lost, limiting examination.
